commentary:
Risk tone is cautiously constructive this morning: equity futures are edging higher (S&P +0.2%, Nasdaq +0.4%, Euro Stoxx +0.2%) and Treasuries have halted their slide as markets settle into a holding pattern ahead of today's Fed decision — traders are pricing a better-than-90% chance of the first hike since 2023, with rates markets already carrying an extreme short and all eyes on the dot plot for how far the Warsh Fed intends to go. UK CPI landed exactly in line at 3.1% headline and 2.6% core, giving gilts room to rally (Long Gilt +0.4%) even as debate builds over whether the BoE is entering its own hiking cycle.

China remains the growth soft spot: August retail sales missed and the investment slump deepened, keeping pressure on Beijing and the PBoC for stimulus. Energy is the complex to watch. Crude is retracing overnight — Brent -1.1% to ~107.50, WTI -1.7% — after a 7.1m-barrel API build and technically overbought conditions, but the distillate story is anything but calm: heating oil and gasoil settled at record highs with cracks near $90-115/bbl as Middle East and Russian supply disruptions intensify and Moscow weighs extending its diesel export ban through October.

Backwardation is steepening across the crude curve, so treat this dip as positioning ahead of the Fed rather than a fundamental turn. Precious metals are catching a bid into the decision — gold +1% at 4,375, silver +1.8% — a hedge against a policy misstep with long-end yields already at cycle highs.
